content.text: : levodopa (dihydroxyphenylalanine) is an amino acid which crosses the BBB and is converted to dopamine (DA) in the brain, thereby replenishing the supply of DA in the basal ganglia; given in a fixed-dose combination with carbidopa which inhibits the peripheral enzyme dopa decarboxylase
: hx of malignant melanoma, narrow-angle glaucoma
: dyskinesias, nightmares, sedation, agitation, hallucinations, delirium, motor fluctuations between mobile & immobile states (“on-off” effect)
MOA:  precursor to DA (DA ⍉cross BBB) -cross BBB
extensive met in GI & periph tissues
Admin: short 1/2 life -off = time when meds ⍉at tx level
MOA: precursor to DA -cross BBB w carbidopa -> less med to get effect
Most clin effective tx for PD Sx
PO: empty stomach: ±30 min b4 meal or ±1 hr after
Levodopa = AA -so- ↑protein/↑fat meals compete w levodopa absorb

-    abnorm invol mvts (dyskinesia)    -    depression    -    psychosis    -    anxiety

: bind to AChE → blocks its action which prevents metabolism of Ach → accumulation of Ach at receptor site → buildup of Ach in synaptic cleft
: inhibit the enzyme AChE, blocking the degradation of ACh, increasing its availability and concentration at all cholinergic receptors (muscarinic and nicotinic)
: GI (N/V/D, abdominal pain), anorexia/weight loss, dizziness, bradycardia, syncope, orthostatic hypotension, QT prolongation
Drug interaction: some AChEIs = CYP substrates
Guidelines: Start low, titrate to target
Pt ed: Gen best tol of AChEIs
